notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase: B often coded course-start for permissions inside syllabus statements where A coded during-work; resolved to during-work because the rule governs how AI is used in assignments, and course-start kept for communication of expectations. (2) actor: A student vs B all on rationale, warning and scope statements; resolved to student when the passage addresses the course's students, all for scope, definitions and facts about university tools. (3) policy_type: approval/permission-before-use templates (P01 vs P10 vs P06) resolved to P01 with fit notes because AI is off unless permitted; required or built-in AI use (P35/P02/P44) resolved to UNCOVERED and recorded as a candidate new type; P24 vs P25 vs P27 for acknowledgment content resolved by what the sentence asks for; one two-use anchor (practice examples / explaining a concept) split into P14 and P12. (4) modality: informs for statements that declare a violation or penalty, must for instructor commitments and stated duties. (5) unit_stance differences on otherwise agreeing units: neutral for informs, else coder A's reading. Coder B coded the CTLA statements and College of Business policy at the end of document 2 that A skipped; kept as real statements. B's cheating-definition unit in the Student Code of Conduct (no AI mention), A's sample-citation example (repeat) and B's restatement of understanding rule were dropped. Matched means same passage by overlapping spans; shares are over matched units.
